title: In Psalms 21 In What Ways Does This Psalm Encourage Us To Trust In Gods Strength Rather Than Our Own
paragraphs: Trusting in God's Strength: Insights from Psalm 21

Psalm 21 is a psalm of David, often classified as a royal psalm, celebrating God's faithfulness in granting victory and blessing to the king. The theme of the psalm is clear: triumph, security, and blessing come not from human might or ingenuity, but from the strength and favor of God. As we explore this passage, we discover several powerful reasons to place our trust in God's strength rather than our own.
1. God as the Source of Victory
David begins by acknowledging that any victory or joy he experiences comes from the Lord:
The king shall joy in thy strength, O Jehovah; And in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice! - Psalm 21:1 ASV

The king (David) does not claim credit for his triumphs. Instead, he rejoices in God's strength and salvation. This teaches us to trace all our successes back to God and to rely on Him for deliverance and victory in every challenge we face.
2. God Grants the Desires of the Heart
David continues:
Thou hast given him his heart’s desire, And hast not withholden the request of his lips. Selah. - Psalm 21:2 ASV

God is attentive to the prayers and desires of His people. Rather than striving in our own strength to fulfill our needs and ambitions, we are encouraged to bring them before God in prayer, trusting His perfect wisdom and timing to answer.
3. Blessings and Honor Come from God
The psalmist rejoices over the blessings and honor bestowed by God:
For thou meetest him with the blessings of goodness: Thou settest a crown of fine gold on his head. - Psalm 21:3 ASV

True honor and blessing are gifts of God’s grace, not the result of our efforts. This encourages us to humbly depend on God for advancement and recognition, rather than seeking to establish ourselves by our own means.
4. God’s Unfailing Love and Presence
A key source of security and strength is God’s steadfast love:
For the king trusteth in Jehovah; And through the lovingkindness of the Most High he shall not be moved. - Psalm 21:7 ASV

Here, David explicitly states his trust is in the Lord, confident that God’s lovingkindness is the foundation for steadfastness and security. Human strength is fleeting, but God’s love is unchanging and sufficient for every need.
5. God’s Judgment Against Enemies
The psalm also reminds us that God is the one who deals with opposition:
For thou wilt make them as a fiery furnace in the time of thine anger: Jehovah will swallow them up in his wrath, And the fire shall devour them. - Psalm 21:9 ASV
Rather than taking vengeance or relying on personal strength against adversaries, the believer can trust in God’s perfect justice and righteous judgment.
6. Praising God for His Strength
The psalm concludes with a call to worship:
Be thou exalted, O Jehovah, in thy strength: So will we sing and praise thy power. - Psalm 21:13 ASV
Our response to God’s strength should be praise and adoration, not self-reliance or pride. We are called to celebrate and honor the power of God in our lives.
Centrality of Trusting God in the Gospel
Ultimately, Psalm 21 points us to the broader biblical truth that salvation and security are found in God alone. As the New Testament echoes:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, that no man should glory. - Ephesians 2:8 ASV
This principle of trusting God’s strength rather than our own is fulfilled most clearly in the gospel of Jesus Christ, who is the ultimate source of victory, blessing, and everlasting security.
Application: How Should We Respond?
Pray: Bring your needs and desires to God, trusting Him to answer according to His will.
Depend: Lean on God’s strength in challenges, rather than your own abilities.
Praise: Regularly praise God for His blessings and victories in your life.
Trust His Justice: Leave matters of opposition and justice in God’s hands.
Conclusion

Psalm 21 invites us to anchor our confidence in the unchanging strength of God, reminding us that every good gift, victory, and blessing comes from His hand. As we trust in Him, we find security, joy, and the freedom to praise Him for all He has done.
